explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/42: for M ≥ 1 and N large in terms of M, does every Sidon A ⊂ {1,…,N} admit a Sidon B ⊂ {1,…,N} of size M with (A−A) ∩ (B−B) = {0}? The Lean statement restricts A to maximal Sidon sets, which is equivalent: any Sidon set extends to a maximal one with a larger difference set, so B for the maximal one also works for A. `A − A` is pointwise subtraction in ℕ, so it is truncated, but this captures nonnegative differences, and those determine the symmetric difference sets, including the 0 forced by nonempty A and B. Faithful.
